description: A group of highschoolers who are interested in aerospace technologies.
summary: Vitals is a self-monitoring prototype that helps astronauts spot changes in radiation exposure, cardiovascular health, immune signs, bone and muscle loading, behavioral health and cabin environment, compare them with their own baseline, and get clear next steps.
details:
Vitals is a self-monitoring web app that helps astronauts on long missions spot changes in their own health when ground contact is delayed. Crew members log a short daily entry (vitals, sleep, exercise, radiation dose, mood, symptoms). Vitals compares it with their own baseline and shows a Nominal, Watch or Act status for six systems: cardiovascular, immune, bone and muscle, behavioral health, radiation, and cabin environment. Each alert says why it fired and what to do next, and a radiation view tracks dose against the 600 mSv career limit and flags possible solar events.

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, running in the browser with data kept on the device, and hosted on Netlify. Code and text were created with Claude (AI).

Status: a prototype with simulated data, a wellness tool and not a medical device. Next: phone and watch sensor data, live NASA space-weather data, and thresholds tuned with flight surgeons.
